Let  
\[
S=\sum_{k=1}^{p-2}\frac{1}{k(k+1)}\pmod p.
\]
Using partial fractions,
\[
\frac{1}{k(k+1)}=\frac1k-\frac1{k+1}.
\]
So the sum telescopes:
\[
S=\left(1-\frac12\right)+\left(\frac12-\frac13\right)+\cdots+\left(\frac1{p-2}-\frac1{p-1}\right)
=1-\frac1{p-1}.
\]
Modulo \(p\), we have \(p-1\equiv -1\), so
\[
\frac1{p-1}\equiv (-1)^{-1}\equiv -1.
\]
Therefore,
\[
S\equiv 1-(-1)=2 \pmod p.
\]

The answer is \(2\).
